explanation: Archaea were once classified as bacteria, but scientists discovered that their ribosomal RNA (rRNA) base sequences differ from those of bacteria. Other key differences include: Archaea cell walls lack peptidoglycan, and their biochemistry is more similar to Eukarya than to Bacteria. Thus, Archaea are now considered more closely related to Eukarya than to Bacteria. Most Archaea are chemoautotrophs. They can form mutualistic or commensalistic relationships, but none are known to be parasitic, and none are photosynthetic.

questions.q: Which of the following is a key difference between Archaea and Bacteria?
opts: Archaea possess cell walls containing peptidoglycan.
Archaea ribosomal RNA base sequences differ from Bacteria, and their cell walls lack peptidoglycan.
Bacteria are biochemical generalists, whereas Archaea are always parasites.
Archaea are photosynthetic, whereas Bacteria are not.
